title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the cote is about dévissage of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures. On these pages Grothendieck sets up the categorical algebra needed to define tensor products and Hom's of 'free module-like' objects with coefficients in an arbitrary additive category.

Setting (previous page). 𝒜 is a '½-additive' category, i.e. a preadditive (Ab-enriched) category that need not have finite direct sums. 𝒞, here renamed 𝒟, is an additive category in which every object is a finite direct sum of objects of 𝒜. In other words 𝒟 is (equivalent to) the additive envelope of 𝒜. It embeds fully faithfully via Yoneda into Hom_{½add}(𝒜°, Ab), the category of right 𝒜-modules, as the finitely generated free modules.

Step 1: restriction is an equivalence. For any additive category 𝒞', restriction along 𝒜 ⊂ 𝒟 gives an equivalence Hom_add(𝒟, 𝒞') ≃ Hom_{½add}(𝒜, 𝒞'). This is the universal property of the additive envelope: an additive functor is determined by its values on summands.

Step 2: the tensor pairing. Choosing a quasi-inverse gives a pairing 𝒟 × Hom_{½add}(𝒜, 𝒞') → 𝒞', with 𝒟 ⊂ Hom_{½add}(𝒜°, Ab). It is written (F, G) ↦ F ⊗ G. In modern terms this is the coend/tensor product of a f.g. free right 𝒜-module F with an 𝒜-shaped diagram G in 𝒞'. On free generators it is h_a ⊗ G = G(a), extended additively.

Step 3: sanity check. When 𝒜 has one object, the ½-additive structure is a ring k. Then F is a free right k-module of finite type, and G is an object of 𝒞' with a k-action, i.e. a left k-module in 𝒞'. F ⊗ G is the ordinary tensor product, namely G^n with the action twisted by a matrix.

Step 4: the dual construction. Embed 𝒞 ≃ 𝒟'° ⊂ Hom_{½add}(𝒜, Ab)°, i.e. as opposites of f.g. free left modules. The same argument gives Hom_add(𝒟'°, 𝒞') ≃ Hom_{½add}(𝒜, 𝒞'). Hence a pairing 𝒟'° × Hom_{½add}(𝒜, 𝒞') → 𝒞'. The next page denotes it Hom_𝒜(F, G): the internal Hom of a free left module into a 𝒞'-valued module, on generators Hom(h^a, G) = G(a).

Purpose. The next page applies this to a category 𝒮 with 𝒞 ⊂ 𝒮_ab and objects X ↦ Hom_𝒮(X, –). The aim is to define tensor/Hom operations on complexes whose components are sums of objects of 𝒜, as groundwork for multiplicative structures on perfect complexes.
errors: Notational slip: the additive category called 𝒞 on the previous page is called 𝒟 here, and the tensor product is subscripted with 𝒞 (F ⊗_𝒞 G). Mathematically it is a tensor product over 𝒜 (equivalently over 𝒟); this is harmless.
The inverse 'foncteur inverse' is only a quasi-inverse, defined up to unique isomorphism, so the pairing is defined up to canonical isomorphism. This is implicit and not an error.
Line-break 'à vérifier' on the previous page: full faithfulness/equivalence in the general Σ'-limit setting is flagged as unchecked. The additive case used here is correct.

ideas.what: Universal property of the additive envelope: additive functors from the category of finite sums of objects of a preadditive 𝒜 equal additive functors from 𝒜.
ideas.modern_name: additive envelope / additive completion (matrix category Mat(𝒜))
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Mitchell 'Rings with several objects' (1972), Freyd

ideas.what: Pairing of f.g. free right 𝒜-modules with 𝒜-diagrams in an additive category, giving F ⊗_𝒜 G.
ideas.modern_name: tensor product of functors / weighted colimit (coend) for Ab-enriched categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan, Yoneda, Mitchell, Kelly (enriched category theory)

ideas.what: Dual pairing giving internal Hom_𝒜(F, G) from free left modules into 𝒞'-valued modules.

ideas.modern_name: preadditive category / ring with several objects

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, correct piece of preadditive/enriched category theory: additive envelope plus coend tensor and its dual Hom, set up as a tool for the dévissage of perfect complexes. The terminology '½-additive' is idiosyncratic, but nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Under the accouplement the subscript reads Hom_{½add}(𝒜°, Ab) (with Ab, 𝒜°); the transcription is essentially right but marked [?].
On the next page 'k-add' is likely a misreading of '½ add' (Hom_{½add}(𝒜, 𝒞') and Hom_{½add}(𝒜, Ab)°).
'avec [?] sa str. ½ add.' likely reads 'donc sa str. ½ add. est définie par un anneau k'.
'G un objet de 𝒞' où k opère' reads approximately 'G un objet de 𝒞' où k opère, i.e. G un k-𝒞'-module à gauche'.
